Commercial and industrial land lease opportunities in Palm Bay are limited — but ground lease structures do exist for the right projects and the right parties.

What Is a Land Lease (Ground Lease)?

A land lease — also called a ground lease — is an arrangement where a landowner allows a tenant to use their land for a specified period in exchange for regular rent payments. The tenant typically builds on the land, and at the end of the lease term, the improvements may revert to the landowner.

Ground leases are common in commercial, industrial, and institutional real estate — particularly for:

  • Retail pad sites and shopping centers
  • Industrial facilities and warehouses
  • Medical office buildings
  • Educational institutions and charter schools
  • Government and municipal facilities
  • Cell tower and utility infrastructure
  • Agricultural and rural uses

Ground leases are NOT common in residential real estate in Palm Bay — with one limited exception discussed below.

Land Lease for Residential in Palm Bay — The Honest Answer

If you are searching for residential land lease in Palm Bay — the honest answer is this is not a standard option in Palm Bay's residential market. There is no residential land leasing program here.

The mobile home situation — what you need to know

Mobile home placement in Palm Bay is significantly more restricted than most people realize. Palm Bay has very limited MH-zoned land within city limits and has not aggressively expanded mobile home designated areas. For practical purposes, MH-zoned land inside Palm Bay is rare and difficult to find.

If you are specifically looking to place a mobile home in the Palm Bay area, here is the honest picture:

  • Mobile homes require MH zoning, rural residential (RR), or agricultural (AU) zoning
  • These zoning designations inside Palm Bay city limits are extremely limited
  • Rural residential and agricultural parcels in unincorporated western Brevard County do exist — but they are rural, away from city infrastructure, and typically 1 acre or more in size
  • Our inventory of rural residential and agricultural parcels is very low
  • Rural residential and agricultural parcels in the Palm Bay area are priced similarly to standard single-family residential lots — there is no significant price advantage
  • Someone looking for a cheap mobile home site in Palm Bay will be disappointed — the economics simply do not work the way people expect

The bottom line on mobile homes in Palm Bay

If mobile home placement is your goal and you want to stay near Palm Bay and the Space Coast, expect to look at rural western Brevard County where prices are lower and land is more abundant. Inside Palm Bay or near the coast, mobile home placement is not a practical or cost-effective option.

The better alternative for most buyers

A standard residential lot with owner financing — owner financing available, no bank required — gives you a site in an established neighborhood at a price point that is genuinely accessible. You own the land and build equity as you pay.

Commercial Land Lease in Palm Bay — What Actually Exists

Commercial ground leases in Palm Bay do exist but they are not a standard listed product. They are typically negotiated privately between landowners and commercial tenants for specific projects.

Solar farms, cell towers, retail pad sites, and medical office buildings are the most common ground lease use cases in Florida — typical lease terms run 25 to 99 years.

When commercial land leases make sense in Palm Bay:

  • Retail Pad Sites: National and regional retailers — fast food chains, pharmacies, banks, and convenience stores — frequently prefer ground leases over purchase for their pad sites. They want to deploy capital into their business operations, not real estate.
  • Medical and Professional Office: Healthcare systems and medical groups frequently use ground leases for clinic and office locations. As Palm Bay's population grows and healthcare demand increases along the Heritage Parkway corridor, medical ground lease opportunities will expand.
  • Cell Tower and Utility Infrastructure: Wireless carriers — AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile — lease land for cell tower placement. These are typically long-term ground leases of 25-50 years on small land footprints.
  • Solar Energy: Utility-scale solar projects lease large land parcels — typically 50-200+ acres — from landowners for 25-35 year terms. Florida Power & Light and other developers actively acquire ground leases for solar farms in rural and semi-rural areas of Brevard and surrounding counties.

Commercial ground lease terms typically include:

  • Initial lease terms of 25-99 years
  • Base rent plus annual escalations (typically 2-3% per year or CPI adjustments)
  • Tenant responsible for all taxes, insurance, and maintenance
  • Reversion clause — improvements revert to landowner at lease end
  • Subordination and non-disturbance agreements for tenant financing

Industrial Land Lease in Palm Bay — The Space Coast Opportunity

Industrial ground leases in Palm Bay and Brevard County are an emerging opportunity driven directly by the Space Coast's aerospace and defense employment boom.

Why industrial tenants seek ground leases

Industrial operators — particularly in aerospace manufacturing, defense contracting, and logistics — often prefer to own their buildings and lease the land underneath. This structure allows them to depreciate the building improvements for tax purposes, retain control of their facility without tying up capital in land, and maintain flexibility as their space needs evolve.

What industrial ground lease tenants are looking for in Palm Bay

  • HI-zoned parcels near I-95 and the St. Johns Heritage Parkway
  • Access to heavy truck corridors
  • Proximity to Space Coast employer campuses
  • Parcels of 5-50+ acres for manufacturing and logistics operations

If you own significant industrial-zoned acreage in Palm Bay and are interested in exploring ground lease structures rather than outright sale — contact us. We have relationships with industrial developers and Space Coast employers who are actively looking for land positions in this market.

Institutional Land Lease in Palm Bay

Institutional users — charter schools, private universities, churches, healthcare systems, and government agencies — represent a steady source of ground lease demand in growing markets.

  • Charter schools: Florida's charter school legislation allows charter schools to count toward school concurrency — meaning developers of large projects like Ashton Park actively need charter school operators. Charter school operators frequently prefer ground lease structures.
  • Healthcare: As Palm Bay's population grows toward and beyond 200,000, healthcare system expansion is inevitable. Hospital systems and clinic operators frequently use ground leases for satellite locations.
  • Religious institutions: Churches and religious organizations frequently seek land in growing residential corridors. Ground lease structures can make sense for faith communities that want to invest in their building rather than land.
  • Government and municipal: City of Palm Bay and Brevard County government facilities — fire stations, community centers, libraries — are occasionally structured as ground leases on privately owned land.

Should You Lease or Buy Land in Palm Bay?

For most buyers and investors in Palm Bay — purchasing land outright is almost always the better financial decision compared to leasing. Here is why:

Buy:

  • You build equity as you pay
  • No landlord — complete control over your property
  • Owner financing available, call for terms. No bank required
  • Annual carrying costs (taxes) are very low on vacant land

Lease:

  • Makes sense for national tenants who deploy capital into operations not real estate
  • Works for institutional users with long planning horizons
  • Appropriate for solar, cell tower, and utility infrastructure
  • Rarely the best option for individual buyers or small investors

If you are an individual buyer or small investor considering land lease vs purchase in Palm Bay — buy. The affordability of Palm Bay land combined with owner financing terms makes outright ownership accessible and financially superior to leasing in almost every scenario.

With lots starting at $41,000 and owner financing available, purchasing land in Palm Bay is more accessible than most buyers realize — and almost always superior to leasing.
